assignmentHtml.task: Audit claims L1 and L2 about JWST. Starting point: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/webb/. Key questions: (1) What did JWST transmission spectroscopy of K2-18 b actually detect? What molecules? (2) Is 'directly photographed organisms' equivalent to 'spectral feature, molecule identification, statistical significance, habitable environment, confirmation of life'? (3) What are the conflicting analyses of possible sulfur-bearing molecules (dimethyl sulfide DMS)? (4) What are the host-star and planetary assumptions, model choices, wavelength coverage, competing analyses? Find the original K2-18 b papers, competing analyses, and discussions of DMS detection limits.
assignmentHtml.context: Mission: James Webb Space Telescope. Target: exoplanet atmosphere characterization, including K2-18 b. Claims L1-L2: L1 says transmission spectroscopy of K2-18 b directly photographed organisms, and spectral feature/molecule/significance/habitable environment/life confirmation are equivalent claims. L2 says conflicting analyses of sulfur-bearing molecule can be resolved by newest press headline alone, and host-star/planetary assumptions, model choices, wavelength coverage, competing analyses need not be explained. These are claims to audit.
assignmentHtml.expected_output: Verdict on each component of L1 and L2 with corrected text, molecules detected, significance levels, competing analyses, source URLs. Clarify what JWST actually found for K2-18 b and how the evidence ladder works.

answerHtml:
Both L1 and L2 are false on every component. L1 conflates transmission spectroscopy with direct imaging and collapses an evidence ladder into a single claim. L2 treats an active, unresolved scientific debate as settleable by press headlines and dismisses necessary context (host-star/planetary parameters, model degeneracies, wavelength coverage, competing analyses). Below is the corrected evidence record.

WHAT JWST ACTUALLY DETECTED IN K2-18b'S ATMOSPHERE

K2-18b is a 2.61 R⊕, 8.63 M⊕ sub-Neptune orbiting an M3V dwarf (T_eff = 3,457 K) at ~120 ly in the habitable zone, discovered 2015 by Kepler. JWST observed it via transmission spectroscopy (starlight passing through the atmosphere during transit) using NIRISS SOSS (0.9–2.8 μm), NIRSpec G395H (2.8–5.2 μm), and later MIRI LRS (5–12 μm).

Confirmed detections:

  • Methane (CH₄): ~5σ in Madhusudhan et al. 2023 (arXiv:2309.05566); confirmed at ~4σ by Schmidt et al. 2025 reanalysis with volume mixing ratio ~1% (range −2.14 ≤ log₁₀(CH₄) ≤ −0.53) [arXiv:2501.18477]. Robustly confirmed again by Hu et al. 2025 combining four new NIRSpec transits with original data [arXiv:2507.12622].
  • Carbon dioxide (CO₂): 3σ in Madhusudhan et al. 2023; robustly confirmed by Hu et al. 2025. However, Schmidt et al. 2025 — a reanalysis using 60 data-reduction variants and >250 retrievals — finds no statistically significant or reliable evidence for CO₂ [arXiv:2501.18477].
  • Ammonia (NH₃): Not detected. Upper limit ~3×10⁻⁵ at 95% confidence (Madhusudhan et al. 2023). Consistent with non-detection in mini-Neptune photochemical models (Wogan et al. 2024) and in Hu et al. 2025.

Tentative/contested:

  • Dimethyl sulfide (DMS) and dimethyl disulfide (DMDS): 'Possible detection' / 'potential signs' in Madhusudhan et al. 2023 (NIR data only, not claimed as a firm detection). Dean-Ben et al. 2024 (ApJ Letters) reported 3σ evidence for DMS from NIR alone. Madhusudhan et al. 2025 (ApJ Letters, April) reported 2.9–3.2σ combined evidence for DMS/DMDS from MIRI 5–12 μm data, with abundances ~10 ppmv (log VMR ≈ −3.3 to −3.5) [ApJL 984, adc1c8]. These claims are actively contested: Schmidt et al. 2025 finds no reliable evidence for DMS; Luque et al. 2025 finds 'insufficient evidence' from a joint panchromatic (0.6–12 μm) analysis using three reduction pipelines and two retrieval codes, noting other methyl-bearing species (e.g., ethane) fit equally well and that ~25 more MIRI transits would be needed for a 3σ rejection of a flat line [arXiv:2505.13407]; Hu et al. 2025 finds only marginal DMS signals (<~2σ without imposing a strong super-Rayleigh haze) and shows abiotic photochemical production of DMS is plausible in H₂-rich, high-metallicity atmospheres [arXiv:2507.12622].

AUDIT OF L1 COMPONENTS

Claim: 'Transmission spectroscopy of K2-18 b directly photographed organisms.' FALSE. JWST performed transmission spectroscopy — analyzing absorption features imprinted on starlight — not direct imaging. No organisms were ever photographed. Source: NASA Webb press release (science.nasa.gov/missions/webb/webb-discovers-methane-carbon-dioxide-in-atmosphere-of-k2-18-b/) and original paper (arXiv:2309.05566).

Claim: 'Spectral feature = molecule identification = statistical significance = habitable environment = confirmation of life.' FALSE — these are distinct evidentiary steps:
(1) A spectral feature is a deviation in the spectrum; interpreting it as a specific molecule requires atmospheric retrieval models that can suffer degeneracy (e.g., DMS vs DMDS vs ethane vs CH₃SH) [Luque et al. 2025].
(2) Molecule identification requires distinguishing among degenerate species; even CH₄ detection at 4–5σ does not uniquely imply biology.
(3) Statistical significance: the DMS/DMDS claims reached at most 2.7–3.2σ [Hu et al. 2025; ApJL adc1c8], well below the 5σ convention for conclusive detection (0.00006% chance of fluke) [astronomy.com].
(4) A habitable environment requires determining whether the planet is a Hycean world (thin H₂ atmosphere over liquid ocean) or a gas-rich mini-Neptune — both interpretations currently fit the data [Wogan et al. 2024; Schmidt et al. 2025].
(5) Confirmation of life requires ruling out abiotic sources; laboratory experiments have demonstrated abiotic DMS formation under simulated exoplanetary conditions [astronomy.com], and photochemical models show DMS can form without biology in massive H₂-rich atmospheres [Hu et al. 2025]. NASA itself states: 'detection of a single potential biosignature would not constitute discovery of life' [science.nasa.gov blog, 2025-04-18].

AUDIT OF L2 COMPONENTS

Claim: 'Conflicting DMS analyses can be resolved by newest press headline alone.' FALSE. As of late 2025 there is no consensus. The timeline shows deepening disagreement:

  • Apr 2023: tentative DMS signs (Madhusudhan et al.) [arXiv:2309.05566]
  • Sep 2024: 3σ DMS from NIR alone (Dean-Ben et al.) [ApJ Letters]
  • Apr 2025: 2.9–3.2σ DMS/DMDS from MIRI (Madhusudhan et al.) [ApJL adc1c8]
  • May 2025: insufficient evidence from joint panchromatic analysis (Luque et al.) [arXiv:2505.13407]; marginal signals, abiotic production possible (Hu et al.) [arXiv:2507.12622]
  • Aug 2025: no reliable DMS evidence in comprehensive reanalysis (Schmidt et al.) [arXiv:2501.18477]
    NASA issued no press release for the April 2025 study, reflecting community uncertainty [astronomy.com].

Claim: 'Host-star/planetary assumptions, model choices, wavelength coverage, competing analyses need not be explained.' FALSE — each is essential:

  • Host-star assumptions: M3V dwarf, high pre-main-sequence XUV flux that could have stripped a primordial H₂ envelope (affecting whether a Hycean atmosphere is even sustainable) [Wogan et al. 2024].
  • Planetary assumptions: mass/radius/density imply H₂-rich envelope; equilibrium temperature ~250–300 K but may approach runaway greenhouse threshold [Wikipedia K2-18b].
  • Model choices: Hycean (requires biosphere for ~1% CH₄ against photochemical destruction) vs. mini-Neptune (thermochemical quenching explains CH₄ without life) — both fit the data with χ²_r ≈ 1.51 [Wogan et al. 2024]. Retrieval frameworks (AURA, petitRADTRANS), data reduction pipelines (JExoRES, JexoPipe), and HITRAN cross-sections for DMS/DMDS (derived at Earth-like STP with N₂ broadening, possibly inaccurate for K2-18b conditions) all affect results [ApJL adc1c8; Luque et al. 2025].
  • Wavelength coverage: NIR (0.9–5.2 μm) constrains CH₄/CO₂; MIRI (5–12 μm) is where DMS/DMDS have strongest features, but the Luque et al. joint analysis shows that preference for DMS in MIR depends on simultaneously fitting NIR data correctly [arXiv:2505.13407].
  • Competing analyses: Wogan et al. 2024 (mini-Neptune), Schmidt et al. 2025 (reanalysis favoring mini-Neptune), Luque et al. 2025 (joint analysis refuting DMS) [see URLs above].

CORRECTED STATEMENT

JWST transmission spectroscopy of K2-18b robustly detected methane (~4–5σ) and (per some analyses) carbon dioxide (~3σ), with ammonia absent. A possible detection of dimethyl sulfide (DMS) at ~2.7–3.2σ has been reported by one group using MIRI data, but multiple independent reanalyses find insufficient or no statistically significant evidence for DMS/DMDS, and abiotic production pathways have been demonstrated. The planet's nature — Hycean ocean world versus gas-rich mini-Neptune — remains genuinely unresolved. None of these findings constitutes confirmation of life.

evidence.snippet: Original Madhusudhan et al. 2023 paper: strong detections of methane (CH4) at 5σ and carbon dioxide (CO2) at 3σ with ~1% volume mixing ratios each in a H2-rich atmosphere; non-detection of ammonia; spectrum suggests potential signs of DMS.
evidence.supports: What JWST originally reported: CH4 at 5σ, CO2 at 3σ, NH3 not detected, DMS only as tentative/potential.

evidence.snippet: Wogan et al. 2024 competing analysis: a lifeless Hycean world is hard to reconcile with ~1% CH4 because photochemistry only supports ppb levels; a gas-rich mini-Neptune with 100× solar metallicity naturally produces 4% CH4 and 0.1% CO2 via thermochemical quenching, fitting the data equally well (χ²_r = 1.51).
evidence.supports: Alternative mini-Neptune interpretation exists; Hycean interpretation requires biogenic CH4; both models fit JWST data.

evidence.snippet: Madhusudhan et al. 2025 (ApJ Letters): MIRI LRS 5–12 μm transmission spectrum detects DMS/DMDS at 2.9σ–3.2σ with abundances ≳10 ppmv; authors note cross-section uncertainties and that sustaining such abundances abiotically would be implausible but not impossible.
evidence.supports: The strongest pro-DMS claim (2.9–3.2σ from MIRI), with acknowledged caveats about cross-sections and abundance assumptions.

evidence.snippet: Schmidt et al. 2025 reanalysis (AJ): using 60 data reductions and >250 retrievals, confirms CH4 at ~4σ but finds no statistically significant or reliable evidence for CO2 or DMS; revised composition explained by oxygen-poor mini-Neptune without requiring ocean or life.
evidence.supports: Comprehensive reanalysis contradicts CO2 and DMS claims; supports non-Hycean interpretation.

evidence.snippet: Luque et al. 2025 (A&A): joint analysis of NIRISS+NIRSpec+MIRI (0.6–12 μm) with three pipelines and two retrieval codes finds insufficient evidence for DMS/DMDS; other methyl-bearing molecules fit equally well; ~25 more MIRI transits needed for 3σ rejection of flat line.
evidence.supports: Joint panchromatic analysis refutes DMS detection claims; highlights model degeneracy and sensitivity to reduction choices.

evidence.snippet: Hu et al. 2025: four new JWST/NIRSpec transits robustly detect CH4 and CO2; DMS, CH3SH, N2O signals only marginal (<3σ, <~2σ without strong haze); abiotic photochemical production of DMS shown possible in H2-rich high-metallicity atmospheres.
evidence.supports: Latest observational update; abiotic DMS pathway demonstrated; reinforces that DMS alone is not a definitive biosignature.

evidence.snippet: Astronomy Magazine summary: NASA issued no press release for the April 2025 DMS study, reflecting uncertainty; abiotic DMS production demonstrated; Hu states DMS on its own may not be a definitive sign of life; Madhusudhan concedes abiotic production possible if planet has a deep atmosphere.
evidence.supports: Community skepticism toward DMS-as-biosignature; NASA's high bar for biosignature claims stated explicitly.

evidence.snippet: NASA official press release: JWST detected methane and carbon dioxide; DMS described as 'possible detection' whose 'inference ... is less robust and requires further validation.'
evidence.supports: Even NASA's own framing treats DMS as unconfirmed and requires further validation — contradicting any claim of life confirmation.

evidence.snippet: NASA blog (2025-04-18): 'detection of a single potential biosignature would not constitute discovery of life. We would need follow-up studies and multiple converging lines of evidence to confirm true biosignatures and rule out false positives.'
evidence.supports: NASA explicitly rejects the equivalence chain: spectral feature → life confirmation.
